topicName: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC): Networks, Subnets, Firewall Rules, Routes
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in Google Cloud (GCP): Networks, Subnets, Firewall Rules, and Routes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network enables you to launch Google Cloud resources in a logically isolated private network. It provides global, scalable, and flexible networking for your cloud-based services. This tutorial covers the core components of a VPC: networks, subnets, firewall rules, and routes."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. VPC Networks"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A VPC network is a global resource that spans all Google Cloud regions. It provides a connected network for your Google Cloud resources. There are two types of VPC networks: default and custom."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"1.1 Default VPC Networks"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Default VPC networks are automatically created when you create a new Google Cloud project. They provide a pre-configured network with a subnet in each region and basic firewall rules. While convenient for initial exploration, they are not recommended for production environments."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"1.2 Custom VPC Networks"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Custom VPC networks offer greater control and flexibility. You define the subnets, IP address ranges, and firewall rules. This allows you to tailor the network to your specific application requirements and security policies."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Example: Creating a custom VPC network using gcloud
gcloud compute networks create my-custom-vpc --subnet-mode custom"},{"order":10,"type":"heading","text":"2. Subnets"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Subnets are regional resources within a VPC network. Each subnet defines a range of IP addresses available for resources in that region. When you create a VM instance, you must specify the subnet where it will reside."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"2.1 Creating Subnets"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"When creating a subnet, you need to specify the VPC network, region, and IP address range (CIDR block). The IP address range must not overlap with other subnets in the same VPC network."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Example: Creating a subnet in the us-central1 region
gcloud compute networks subnets create my-subnet \
    --network my-custom-vpc \
    --region us-central1 \
    --range 10.10.10.0/24"},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"3. Firewall Rules"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Firewall rules control network traffic to and from your VM instances. They are defined at the VPC network level and apply to all instances within that network. You can create firewall rules to allow or deny traffic based on source IP address, destination IP address, protocol, and port."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"3.1 Creating Firewall Rules"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"When creating a firewall rule, you need to specify the direction of traffic (ingress or egress), the action (allow or deny), the source or destination IP address range, the protocol, and the port. You can also specify target tags to apply the rule to specific instances."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"# Example: Allowing ingress traffic on port 80 from any source
gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-http \
    --network my-custom-vpc \
    --allow tcp:80 \
    --source-ranges 0.0.0.0/0 \
    --direction INGRESS"},{"order":20,"type":"heading","text":"4. Routes"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Routes define the path that network traffic takes from a VM instance to a destination. Each VPC network has a default route that sends all traffic to the internet gateway. You can create custom routes to override the default route and direct traffic to specific destinations, such as other VPC networks or on-premises networks."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"4.1 Creating Routes"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"When creating a route, you need to specify the destination IP address range, the next hop (e.g., an internet gateway, a VM instance, or a VPN tunnel), and a priority. The route with the highest priority (lowest number) will be used."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"# Example: Creating a route to send traffic to a specific IP range through a gateway
gcloud compute routes create my-route \
    --network my-custom-vpc \
    --destination-range 192.168.1.0/24 \
    --next-hop-gateway default-internet-gateway"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding and configuring VPC networks, subnets, firewall rules, and routes is crucial for building secure and scalable applications on Google Cloud. By using custom VPC networks and carefully configuring these components, you can create a network environment that meets your specific requirements."}]
